hypothesis: A two-chart polar atlas of the sphere with exact transitions integrates great circles through or near a pole with an accuracy that does not depend on how close they pass, while a single polar chart loses accuracy or fails near its poles.
input_data: unit sphere; great circles with closest approach delta in [0.0, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-06, 1e-08, 1e-10, 1e-12] to the north pole, azimuth 1.3, full length 2 pi
mathematical_model: Chart A: X = R(sin t cos p, sin t sin p, cos t); chart B = R_y(pi/2) X_A, poles on A's equator. det g / R^4 = sin^2 theta in each chart and sin^2 theta_A + sin^2 theta_B = 1 + y^2/R^2 >= 1, so the better chart always has det g / R^4 >= 1/2. Transitions: u_B = X_B^{-1}(X_A(u_A)), v_B = g_B^{-1} J_B^T J_A v_A.
numerical_result: atlas through the pole: error 4.86e-08, 4 switches (A->B, B->A, A->B, B->A); atlas error spread over delta 1.21x; orders 4.16, 3.96; single chart failed for 4 and degraded (>10x atlas) for 7 of 8 delta > 0; exact meridian in chart A alone: error 7.42e-14; transitions round trip 6.5e-16, speed 5.25e-16, Jacobian 3.72e-10; covering bound 0.502.
observation_model: Ambient error max_s |X_num(s) - X_exact(s)|; exact great circle cos(s) X0 + sin(s) T0.

uncertainty: Atlas errors are RK4 truncation errors (order 4). Single-chart errors for small delta come from the unresolved azimuthal rate 1/sin(delta) at a fixed step; the failure steps and the errors for delta <= 1e-8 depend on rounding and may differ across platforms.
unresolved_assumptions: Only the sphere has an atlas here; other surfaces need their own charts and transitions.
Switching happens between steps; an adaptive integrator would need event location at the threshold.
